alignments.note: Closest points between (x-5)^2+(y-4)^2=4 and (x-1)^2+(y-1)^2=1 — centre/radius plus the distance-between-centres reading.

alignments.title: Given two lines crossing a circle, can we show these lengths are equal?
cieTitles: interpret and use any of the forms y = mx + c , y – y = m ( x – x ) , ax + by + c = 0 in solving
alignments.note: Lines through circle points S, T, U, V on x^2+(y-c)^2=r^2; substitution gives quadratics in s and t; p+q=0 — substituting lines into the circle equation is 1.3.2; the STEP III proof depth is extension (recorded medium).

alignments.title: What's the locus of $(p, q)$ if the length of this tangent equals $p$?
cieTitles: interpret and use any of the forms y = mx + c , y – y = m ( x – x ) , ax + by + c = 0 in solving
alignments.note: AP=3PB locus is the circle S tangent to the y-axis; tangent-length locus equidistant from a line and a point — the locus-to-circle family; the parabola locus is extension vocabulary.
